brief: Measures how alike two vectors are: cosine similarity, Euclidean and Manhattan distance, dot product, and the length and unit form of one vector.
detail: Build one with new stzSimilarity() or StzSimilarityQ(); it holds nothing, so it is a bundle of calculations done in the Zig engine. The methods ending in 3 take six numbers, for two 3-component vectors; the ones ending in FromLists, and their short names Cosine, Euclidean, Manhattan and Dot, take two lists of any length, 1,536 for a sentence embedding included, and refuse lists of different lengths. The global functions CosineSimilarity3, EuclideanDistance3, ManhattanDistance3 and DotProduct3 do the 3-component case without an object. Cosine is 1 for the same direction, 0 for perpendicular, -1 for opposite.
